{{Short description|Conjecture in geometry}}

In [[geometry]], the '''Egan conjecture''' gives a [[Necessity and sufficiency|sufficient and necessary condition]] for the [[Radius|radii]] of two [[N-sphere|spheres]] and the distance of their centers, so that a [[simplex]] exists, which is completely contained inside the larger sphere and completely encloses the smaller sphere. The [[conjecture]] generalizes an [[Equation|equality]] discovered by [[William Chapple (surveyor)|William Chapple]] (and later independently by [[Leonhard Euler]]), which is a special case of [[Poncelet's closure theorem]], as well as the [[Grace–Danielsson inequality]] in one [[dimension]] higher.

The conjecture was proposed in 2014 by the Australian mathematician and science-fiction author [[Greg Egan]]. The "sufficient" part was proved in 2018, and the "necessary" part was proved in 2023.

== Basics ==
For an arbitrary triangle (<math>2</math>-simplex), the radius <math>r</math> of its [[inscribed circle]], the radius <math>R</math> of its [[circumcircle]] and the distance <math>d</math> of their centers are related through [[Euler's theorem in geometry]]:

: <math>d^2=R(R-2r)</math>,

which was published by [[William Chapple (surveyor)|William Chapple]] in 1746<ref name=":16">{{citation|author=Chapple, William|editor=Miscellanea Curiosa Mathematica|pages=117–124, formula on the bottom of page 123|title=An essay on the properties of triangles inscribed in and circumscribed about two given circles (1746)|volume=4}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> and by [[Leonhard Euler]] in 1765.<ref name=":17">{{citation|author=Leversha, Gerry; Smith, G. C.|date=November 2007|editor=The Mathematical Gazette|pages=436–452|title=Euler and triangle geometry|volume=91}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

For two spheres (<math>2</math>-spheres) with respective radii <math>r</math> and <math>R</math>, fulfilling <math>r<R</math>, there exists a (non-regular) [[tetrahedron]] (<math>3</math>-simplex), which is completely contained inside the larger sphere and completely encloses the smaller sphere, if and only if the distance <math>d</math> of their centers fulfills the [[Grace–Danielsson inequality]]:

: <math>d^2\leq(R+r)(R-3r)</math>.

This result was independently proven by [[John Hilton Grace]] in 1917 and G. Danielsson in 1949.<ref name=":13">{{citation|author=Grace, J.H.|date=1918|editor=Proc. London Math.|pages=259–271|title=Tetrahedra in relation to spheres and quadrics|volume=Soc.17}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref name=":14">{{citation|author=Danielsson, G.|date=1952|editor=Johan Grundt Tanums Forlag|pages=101–105|title=Proof of the inequality d2≤(R+r)(R−3r) for the distance between the centres of the circumscribed and inscribed spheres of a tetrahedron}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> A connection of the inequality with [[Quantum information|quantum information theory]] was described by Anthony Milne.<ref name=":15">{{cite journal|author=Anthony Milne|date=2014-04-02|language=en|title=The Euler and Grace-Danielsson inequalities for nested triangles and tetrahedra: A derivation and generalisation using quantum information theory|journal=Journal of Geometry |volume=106 |issue=3 |pages=455–463 |doi=10.1007/s00022-014-0257-8 |arxiv=1404.0525 }}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

== Conjecture ==
Consider <math>n</math>-dimensional euclidean space <math>\mathbb R^n</math> for <math>n\geq 2</math>. For two <math>n-1</math>-[[N-sphere|spheres]] with respective radii <math>r</math> and <math>R</math>, fulfilling <math>r<R</math>, there exists a <math>n</math>-[[simplex]], which is completely contained inside the larger sphere and completely encloses the smaller sphere, if and only if the distance <math>d</math> of their centers fulfills:

: <math>d^2\leq(R+(n-2)r)(R-nr)</math>.

The conjecture was proposed by [[Greg Egan]] in 2014.<ref name=":18">{{cite web|access-date=2023-11-22|author=John Baez|date=2014-07-01|language=en|title=Grace–Danielsson Inequality|url=https://blogs.ams.org/visualinsight/2014/06/01/grace-danielsson-inequality/}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

For the case <math>n=1</math>, where the inequality reduces to <math>d\leq R-r</math>, the conjecture is true as well, but trivial. A <math>0</math>-sphere is just composed of two points and a <math>1</math>-simplex is just a closed [[Interval (mathematics)|interval]]. The desired <math>1</math>-simplex of two given <math>0</math>-spheres can simply be chosen as the closed interval between the two points of the larger sphere, which contains the smaller sphere if and only if it contains both of its points with respective distance <math>|d-r|</math> and <math>d+r</math> from the center of the larger sphere, hence if and only if the above inequality is satisfied.

== Status ==
Greg Egan showed that the condition is sufficient in comments on a blog post by [[John C. Baez|John Baez]] in 2014. The comments were lost in a rearrangement of the website, but the central parts were copied into the original blog post. Further comments by Greg Egan on 16 April 2018 concern the search for a generalized conjecture involving [[ellipsoid]]s.<ref name=":18" /> Sergei Drozdov published a paper on [[ArXiv]] showing that the condition is also necessary in October 2023.<ref name=":19">{{cite arXiv | last=Drozdov | first=Sergei | date=16 October 2023 | title=Egan conjecture holds |eprint=2310.10816 |class=math.MG}}</ref>
